title: Cache reservoir quantization smoke test: FP8 / INT8 / INT4 fidelity vs throughput
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Goal: Measure real-world trade-offs between FP8/INT8/INT4 compression of the KV cache and end-to-end QoE under continuous batching and realistic request mixes. We want a reproducible smoke test that captures both tail latency and generation-quality regressions for representative customers and workloads.

Motivation: KV cache is the dominant GPU memory consumer for mid/long-context LLM workloads. Aggressive quantization can reduce memory footprint enough to increase batch sizes or fit bigger models on a GPU, but we need concrete signals about when quality degradation becomes user-visible and how batching patterns interact with quantized decoding. Existing experiments focus on microbenchmarks and synthetic workloads; this ticket runs a pipeline-level probe across cohorts and batching regimes.

Hypotheses:
1) FP8 preserves fidelity for most prompts at 1–2% end-task metric loss while reducing KV memory ~2x relative to FP16 for the target layer layout.
2) INT8 yields ~3–5% median quality delta but enables ~2.5–3x cache compression with predictable degradation patterns concentrated on factual-recall tokens.
3) INT4 shows non-linear failures on long-coherence contexts (>= 1024 tokens) unless augmented with residual compensation or cohort-specific recalibration.
4) Continuous batching increases effective effective token reuse; combined with KV compression, cache-hit VS decompress cost trades off differently for low-latency (SLO) routes vs throughput-optimized routes.

Experiment plan:
- Workloads: three representative cohorts: (A) interactive chat (short turns, low latency), (B) summarization (long contexts, high reuse), (C) search/embedding+rerank (mixed).
- Models: llama-2-13b and an LLM surrogate previously used by infra benchmarks (model variants pinned to runtime-1.18 profiles).
- Compression modes: FP8 (e4m3-style), INT8 symmetric per-slab, INT4 block-wise with per-block scale and a residual-correction pass (fast approx). Also baseline FP16 (no compression).
- Batching regimes: steady-state continuous batching at target batch sizes [1, 4, 16], and bursty arrivals simulated by Poisson bursts. Measure prefix KV hits and effective batch amortization.
- Metrics: end-task quality (BLEU/ROUGE where applicable, and a set of prompt-based factuality checks), generation divergence (token-level KL and perplexity shift), P50/P90/P99 latency for cold and warm starts, GPU memory footprint, and CPU/GPU decompression overhead.
- Validation harness: use existing eval harness from infra-evals; add per-cohort prompt sets and golden responses; store per-request diffs and sample traces for manual triage.

Success criteria / abort conditions:
- Success: FP8 shows <=1.5% median end-task regression vs FP16 while reducing KV memory >=1.8x and not increasing P99 tail latency more than 10% under continuous batching workloads.
- Abort/rollback: any quant mode that introduces >7% high-severity factual error rate increase on cohort B (summarization) compared to baseline, or causes P99 latency regressions >30% on interactive cohort A.

Deliverables:
- Smoke test harness checked into infra-experiments with clear flags to switch model, cohort, and quant mode.
- Dashboard capturing per-cohort metrics and per-token divergence heatmaps.
- Short results memo with recommended guardrail thresholds for runtime fallback policies (e.g., per-customer hysteresis thresholds for: switch to higher-fidelity cache when factual-error-rate delta > X for 200 consecutive requests).

Resources & runtime impact:
- Allocate a dedicated experiment DGX slot (2x A100 equivalent) for the probing runs for up to 48 hours.
- Need one infra engineer (assignee) and one RE/QA for prompt set curation.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: synthetic prompt sets miss customer edge cases. Mitigation: seed cohorts with anonymized real traces (approved by privacy) and a stratified sample of failing sessions from incident logs.
- Risk: decompression CPU cost dominates gains at small batch sizes. Mitigation: measure decompression in isolation and include optimized kernels in follow-up if promising.

Notes: this ticket is intentionally lightweight — a smoke test to decide whether to escalate to a full cohort-level A/B. If results are promising, follow-ups will include per-shard quant calibration and a runtime fallback implement in the smart router (policy-driven).
acceptance_criteria: Smoke harness runs end-to-end for all three cohorts and all quant modes without runtime crashes
Dashboard shows per-cohort P50/P90/P99 and end-task quality deltas for each quant mode
Clear recommendation: either FP8 safe for canary (with thresholds) OR a decision to iterate on hybrid residual compensation
Artifacts: link to PR, experiment notebook, and raw exports stored in /experiments/kv-quant-smoke
